headline: Recommended six bond authorizations, including $9,000,000 for an ERP system and $3,000,000 for Nashua Public Library renovation.
summary: Much of the discussion focused on whether the unsettled library workers' contract should affect the library bond. The finance chief said the ERP system would cost about $15 million over 10 years. Alderman Johnson opposed four of the bonds.
decisions: Recommended final passage of bonds not to exceed $5,173,428 for purchase of capital equipment; motion carried with Alderman Johnson opposed.
Recommended final passage of bonds not to exceed $3,000,000 for design and other costs to renovate the Nashua Public Library; motion carried.
Recommended final passage of bonds not to exceed $1,500,000 for design, construction and equipping of a fire training facility; motion carried with Alderman Johnson opposed.
Recommended final passage of bonds not to exceed $1,000,000 for design and other costs to replace the Pine Hill Fire Station; motion carried with Alderman Johnson opposed.
Recommended final passage of bonds not to exceed $1,000,000 for deferred capital maintenance of fire stations; motion carried with Alderman Johnson opposed.
Recommended final passage of bonds not to exceed $9,000,000 to replace and modernize the city-wide ERP system; motion carried, and Alderman Sennott said he voted no.

BUDGET REVIEW COMMITTEE 
 
OCTOBER 26, 2026 
 
A meeting of the Budget Review Committee was held Monday, October 26, 2026 at 8:57 p.m. in the Aldermanic Chamber 
and duly noticed in two places, including the City’s website, in accordance with the requirements of RSA 91 -A:2 II. 
 
Alderman Richard A. Dowd, Chairman, presided. 
 
Let’s start the meeting by taking a roll call attendance.   
 
Members of Committee present: Alderman-at-Large Michael B. O’Brien, Sr. 
 Alderwoman-at-Large Shoshanna Kelly 
 Alderman-at-Large Alicia Gregg 
 Alderman Derek Thibeault

Members not in Attendance:

ROLL CALL 
 
PUBLIC COMMENT  
 
Tom Kelly, Fire Commissioner 
 
Good evening everyone.  I’m Tom Kelly, Board of Nashua Fire Commission.  I want to speak to the four resolutions being 
presented to you tonight that were also presented in the last meeting.   
 
The Board of Fire Commissioners recognizes that every capital request competes for limited taxpayer resources.  Our 
responsibility is to distinguish between what would be nice to have and what is genuinely necessary to maintain a safe , 
effective, and professional fire department.  These four initiatives represent essential investments in public safety, 
infrastructure, and operational readiness.  All four initiatives have been approached, and thoroughly balanced, 
operational necessity with responsible capital planning, and stewardship of taxpayer resources.  The Board of Fire 
Commissioners, as by the documents contained in your packet, support these resolutions and respectfully encourage the 
Committee’s favorable consideration.  Thank you.  
 
Chairman Dowd 
 
Thank you.   Anyone else for Public Comment?  Seeing none.  Moving on.

Chairman Dowd 
 
Before we get into the Resolutions, if we could try to the best of our ability to refrain from asking the same the questions

fine, but to move things along and if you have new things, of course, bring them up.

ON THE QUESTION  
 
Alderwoman Kelly  
 
Thank you.  It’s a weird place to put this but I’m gonna ask it.  So if - my question is to Director Enwright, Dawn – you’re 
not a Director, sorry.  So I have the bond plan that we worked through this summer in front of us  and for example, I 
looked at this trend and I thought it was interesting.  So you’re asking for the full amount for ERP – it’s actually a million 
dollars less than we talked about.  We approved the full amount for DPW Garage but then you look at like at your re quest 
for the Library, it’s a $44 million dollar project but we’re only asking for 3.  One of the colleagues in our chamber also 
asked why are we bonding a million for fire deferred maintenance where the actual overall request is $7.5 million.  So 
why were some projects requested full and some requested partial? 
 
Chairman Dowd 
 
Director Cummings.  
 
Tim Cummings, Director of Administrative Services  
 
Yup, thank you.  I know that was directed at CFO Enwright but I thought it might be better for me to answer that specific 
question.  Tim Cummings, Director of Administrative Services.  And the answer to the question is – it harkens back to 
something we heard a couple years ago where we heard that school building projects and t hen also municipal building 
projects/general government building projects really - there was an appetite to have a better understanding and clarity of 
what the construction cost number would be before we authorized funding.  So we started out developing th is incremental 
or phased approach for the building projects doing design, getting a better understanding of what the building project 
would be once we completed design, and then authorizing the construction projects based off of the design as 
developed.  So that is why not only the Fire Station, but the Library, the DPW garage all have taken a phased approach 
to the building projected instead of us authorizing the construction or the total project cost all at once.  Thank you. 
 
Alderwoman Kelly 
 
Follow up, please?
Budget Review Committee – 10/26/2026   Page 3 
 
Chairman Dowd 
 
Just one amplification.  During the design phase, you do all the different levels of drawings to the effect you get to the 
construction drawings.  The contractor that’s going to make the building use the construction drawings to ac tually price 
out what the project is going to cost from a construction standpoint.  I think that’s what Director Cummings was trying to 
point out.  Go ahead.

bonding a million dollars.  So you’re asking us for a million dollars in a couple of these scen arios where the total picture is 
you’re actually asking for $7.5 or whatever.  So I do think that that has to be addressed when people are asking, “I 
thought we weren’t gonna bond $1.5 million or I thought we weren’t gonna do this” when the total project cost isn’t the 
$1.5 million.   
 
Tim Cummings, Director of Administrative Services  
 
If I may? 
 
Chairman Dowd 
 
Yes, Director Cummings.   
 
Tim Cummings, Director of Administrative Services 
 
That’s an excellent point.  I was actually sitting in the seat thinking about that when I heard the conversation. I’m mean 
I’m making this up but certainly, we could authorize $10 million dollars over a 10 year period and do $1 million dollars of 
debt selling for certain deferred capital maintenance program.  I mean that is one way we could look to do it.  
 
To your point, you know, if they’re saying the numbers are like $7 - $7.5 million.  I think school is probably something 
more like $9 – $9.5 million.  We could ask for that all up front and know that that’s for a ce rtain period of years and we 
would be looking to authorize that money knowing that the money would be spent over that period of time.   
 
There’s a couple constraints I just want to kind of point out.  One - we can only spend the money so fast so you certainly 
could authorize the money but we can only do so many projects in a year.  So that’s one thing that we need to be 
cognizant of.  
 
The second is, is the numbers do change and they do fluctuate and by us taking this approach , it actually gives you more 
control and you could actually be a little bit more deliberative in how you want to approach it.  But certainly , we could 
come at it from the other way and we could look at doing that if that’s of interest.  Thank you.  
 
Chairman Dowd 
 
Follow up?   
 
Alderwoman Kelly  
 
Just a response.  I think that this an interesting way of going about it but we also could end up bonding money for a 
project that no longer has an appetite and now we have to re-bond that money to do the design phase because it’s 
pushed out 10 years.   
 
Chairman Dowd  
 
Alderman Clemons.  
 
Alderman Clemons  
 
Thank you.  Well to just to that very last point.  I mean if we have a design, we can always implement it later because we 
have the design.  That wouldn’t change.
Budget Review Committee – 10/26/2026   Page 4 
 
But my point was though even if we were to do like for example the whole fire station if we were to completely bond that 
out, including the design, isn’t true that we wouldn’t bond – we wouldn’t take out the entire bond, right?  We’d only take 
out the portion that we were financing for the architectural design, correct?   
 
Tim Cummings, Director of Administrative Services  
 
That’s correct.  There’s a fundamental difference between authorization – Tim Cummings, Director of Administrative 
Services.  There's a difference between authorizing the bond and then selling of the debt and we would only sell what we 
use.   
 
Alderman Clemons 
 
Right.  So whether we do this in two different phases or not, we’d still be in the same situation essentially.   
 
Chairman Dowd 
 
There’s one other point I want to make that I’ll state and then have Ms. Enwright baptize it.  If we authorize a large 
amount of money and as soon as we start spending it – well first of all, most of the time we pay our invoices out of cash 
and then when we need the cash replacement, we issue the bonds in the most favorable time to buy the bonds.  But 
once we buy the bonds on a large project, there’s a certain amount of time we have to sell that entire bond.  So it’s safer 
doing it the way we’re doing it than to authorize the entire amount because we’ll have to sell those bonds sooner than we 
want to – and she’s nodding her head so.  Any other questions?  Alderman Klee.  
 
Alderman Klee 
 
Thank you, Mr. Chairman.  Adding on to what Director Cummings had added.  I remember sitting here in this chamber 
when people have come up and said “How can you ask for $15 million or $20 million dollars when you haven’t even done 
the design, and you haven’t done this and so on?”  I don’t want to kind of put salt in a wound but I think the Performing 
Arts Center is kind of one of those things that happened.  We got an initial this is what we guesstimate it to be cost.  We 
said this is what the bond was going to be and it ended up being a little bit higher because when actual de sign came 
through, it was proven that way.  So I don’t want to go down that road again.  I would rather have design cost pay for that 
and then move forward with whether or not we really want to go forward.  I know some people would say “Well, you’ve 
already spent $1 million dollars”.  Well I’ve spent $1 million dollars, or $2 million dollars, or whatever it is that I’ve spent 
but I haven’t spent the $20 million, or the $9 million, or the $3 million.  So I think it is the better way to do it, so.  
 
Chairman Dowd 
 
Any other questions?  Alderman Sullivan.  
 
Alderman Sullivan 
 
More of a comment but just to play Devil’s Advocate because I am in favor actually.  I’ve thought about this.  I’d rather 
have one conversation as opposed to four but when you look at how we budget and the way we supplementally 
appropriate, I mean what we’re doing and what we’ve done over the past couple of weeks is we’ve added to the budget.  
So when we come back in Fiscal Year ‘28, the denominator is higher and when you apply that for the spending cap, 
you’re gonna have more room under the cap.  That’s what we’re doing.  So that to me is kind of a byproduct of why I 
don’t like doing this but to play Devil’s Advocate, I guess I would rather go and stair step it as opposed to doing this 
because then it’s gonna give you a lot of room under the cap and then when you have the room , then you’re probably 
gonna use it.  So just playing Devil’s Advocate on that so.  
 
Chairman Dowd 
 
Any other questions?  Seeing none.
